findings.explanation: In Helm 3, `helm list` by default returns only releases that are deployed or failed, and only in the current namespace. A job running the command as written never emits `pending-install`, `pending-upgrade` or `pending-rollback` releases, so the stuck-release half of the detection is silently blind. Helm 4 changed the default to all statuses, but Helm 3 is still the common install base.
findings.quote: Ingest Helm release status from `helm list -o json` jobs
findings.suggested_fix: Specify `helm list --all --all-namespaces -o json` (or `-a -A`), run on a schedule by a scripted input with a kubeconfig that can read release secrets in every namespace. Note that Helm 4 lists all statuses by default.

findings.explanation: Flux helm-controller does not report Helm status strings. HelmRelease health is shown through `.status.conditions`, for example `type: Ready`, `status: "False"`, `reason: InstallFailed | UpgradeFailed | RollbackFailed | TestFailed`. The UC does not say how to turn these conditions into the `status` values (`failed`, `pending-upgrade` and so on) the search expects.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the mapping explicitly: Ready=False with an InstallFailed, UpgradeFailed, RollbackFailed, UninstallFailed or TestFailed reason maps to `failed`, and Reconciling=True for more than N minutes maps to `pending`. Say whether the mapping is done at ingest (props/transforms) or in the search.

findings.explanation: Neither sourcetype is produced by a named add-on, and the UC does not describe their shape. `helm list -o json` emits a JSON array with keys `name`, `namespace`, `revision`, `updated`, `status`, `chart`, `app_version`. It has no `release` or `message` key, so a reader cannot match fields to the grouping in the search. Flux controller logs come from the Kubernetes container log pipeline (for example the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector), not a Universal Forwarder modular input.
findings.quote: `sourcetype=helm:release`, `sourcetype=fluxcd:controller` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Describe each feed: (1) a scripted input that runs `helm list -a -A -o json` and splits the array into one event per release as `helm:release`, renaming `name` to `release` if the search keeps that field. (2) Flux helm-controller container logs collected by the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes and assigned `fluxcd:controller`.

findings.explanation: There is no threshold in the SPL. Any release in a failed or pending state is returned. The description never states what an unhealthy release is.
findings.quote: Outputs `values` each `the scheduled window`; alert when configured threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: lists every Helm release, from Helm CLI polls or Flux HelmRelease logs, whose latest status is failed, pending-install, pending-upgrade or pending-rollback. Show one row per release, namespace, chart and status with the last event time and messages.

findings.explanation: Template text with no real Helm causes. Real benign hits include pending states seen during an in-progress `helm upgrade --wait` or `--atomic` run, a failed revision that a later successful upgrade has already replaced (if old events stay in the search window), and releases being deliberately uninstalled.
findings.quote: Planned work for 'Helm Release Health Monitoring' shifts `values` over `span=1h`
findings.suggested_fix: List those causes. Recommend evaluating only the latest event per release and namespace, and requiring a pending state to persist across at least two polls before alerting.

findings.explanation: The search uses no cluster metrics, so the collector is listed for a capability this UC does not use.
findings.suggested_fix: List the OpenTelemetry Collector only as the carrier of Flux controller logs, or remove it.

findings.explanation: The text is vague and never says the UC flags software installs or upgrades that failed or got stuck halfway.
findings.quote: We watch Kubernetes release tooling so manifest or chart problems surface before users do.
findings.suggested_fix: For example: 'When an install or upgrade of an application on our clusters fails or gets stuck halfway, we flag it so the team can fix or roll it back.'

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The Flux branch `kind="HelmRelease"` is unlikely to match. Flux controller logs carry `controllerKind` and `HelmRelease.name`/`namespace` fields, and have no `status`, `release` or `chart` values. Because `stats ... by release, namespace, chart, status` drops rows with any null by-field, Flux events can never produce results. Check against real helm-controller log events.

The status filter omits `pending-install` and `uninstalling`. Results are also grouped by status rather than by latest state per release, so a release that failed and was later upgraded successfully still appears.

summary: The implementation line is the only UC-specific text, and it has a Helm 3 behaviour gap: plain `helm list` hides pending releases. It also never explains how Flux HelmRelease conditions map to the Helm status strings the SPL filters on. The remaining prose fields are template text.
